paragraphs.text: Why not take the bike and try one of these wonderful cycling routes next weekend?
paragraphs.translation: 何不骑上自行车，在下个周末尝试其中一条绝佳的骑行路线呢？

paragraphs.text: A Bo'ness to Blackness Castle, Edinburgh
paragraphs.translation: A 博内斯至布莱克尼斯城堡路线，爱丁堡

paragraphs.text: If you like cycling on flat ground and enjoy having interesting things to look at, this is one of the best trails in Scotland, Among its plus points, there are fantastic views of three of the bridges across the river Forth, Simply return by the same path or continue on to South Queensferry for a longer day out.
paragraphs.translation:
如果你喜欢在平坦的地面上骑行，并乐于欣赏有趣的景致，这是苏格兰最好的骑行路线之一。
其优点之一是可以欣赏到横跨福斯河的三座桥梁的壮观景色。
只需沿原路返回，或继续前往南昆斯费里，享受更长的户外时光。

paragraphs.text: B The Montgomery Canal cycle path, Wales
paragraphs.translation: B 蒙哥马利运河自行车道，威尔士

paragraphs.text: Dragonflies, swans, buzzards, fish and other creatures can be spotted as you cycle alongside the canal. The path is in good condition and broad enough for a family to ride safely, A day out cycling in the area can also include a visit to the nearby thirteenth-century Powis Castle and its beautiful gardens.
paragraphs.translation:
在运河边骑行时，你可以看到蜻蜓、天鹅、鵟、鱼和其他生物。
这条道路状况良好，且足够宽阔，可以供一家人安全骑行；在该地区骑行一天，还可以顺道参观附近的十三世纪波伊斯城堡及其美丽的花园。

paragraphs.text: C A walking and cycling path in Birmingham, West Midlands
paragraphs.translation: C 西米德兰兹郡伯明翰的一条步行与骑行路径

paragraphs.text: The busy city of Birmingham has several well-known bike trails, including a quiet route along the Bourn Brook to Woodgate Valley country park. One hump-backed bridge is best walked across, but the rest of the route is flat and suitable for a range of bikes. It's then 2km along the signposted path to Woodgate Valley, which is perfect for picnics, has a family-friendly visitor attraction especially known for its sheep, and offers a break from cycling.
paragraphs.translation:
繁忙的伯明翰市拥有几条著名的自行车道，其中包括一条沿着伯恩溪通往伍德盖特谷乡村公园的安静路线。
一座拱形桥最好推车步行通过，但其余路段平坦，适合各种自行车骑行。
然后沿着有路标的小径骑行2公里即可到达伍德盖特谷，那里非常适合野餐，设有一个以羊群闻名的家庭友好型景点，并能让您从骑行中得到休息。

paragraphs.text: D The Cycle Trail in the Forest of Dean, Gloucestershire
paragraphs.translation: D 格洛斯特郡迪恩森林的自行车道

paragraphs.text: The path is on a former railway route from the time when the area was involved in coal mining. Cyclists can visit sites from this period on the way, but those just along for the views won't be disappointed. Stop for lunch at one of the numerous picnic spots along the way, The route is circular, fully marked and suitable for the whole family, including the dog.
paragraphs.translation:
这条路径位于一条昔日的铁路线上，源自该地区从事煤炭开采的时期。
骑行者沿途可以参观这一时期的遗址，但仅为了风景而来的人也不会失望。
在沿途众多野餐点之一停下来享用午餐，这条路线是环形的，标识清晰，适合全家出游，包括狗在内。

paragraphs.text: E The Wirral Trail, Liverpool
paragraphs.translation: E 利物浦威勒尔小径

paragraphs.text: The trail is safe, flat and with plenty of cafés on the way. Take in the views of North Wales, have a rest on the beach at Caldy or Thurstaston, then cross the border into Cheshire and on towards Chester. Both West Kirby and Chester have regular direct trains back to Liverpool.
paragraphs.translation:
这条路线安全、平坦，沿途还有许多咖啡馆。
欣赏北威尔士的景色，在卡尔迪或瑟斯塔斯顿的海滩上休息，然后跨越边界进入柴郡，继续向切斯特前进。
西柯比和切斯特都有直达利物浦的定期火车。

paragraphs.text: What steps to take to become a fashion designer
paragraphs.translation: 成为一名时装设计师需要采取哪些步骤

paragraphs.text: First, it's important to think about what types of fashion designers are in demand currently. There are so many womenswear designers, yet not as many menswear sportswear or accessories designers. Opportunities might be greater in those categories.
paragraphs.translation:
首先，思考当前哪些类型的时装设计师有需求是很重要的。
女装设计师非常多，但男装、运动服或配饰设计师却没有那么多。
这些类别中的机会可能更大。

paragraphs.text: When applying for internships, think about what you'll bring to the company as well as what they can offer you: ls the company going to teach you skills that are relevant to your future career? What mix of skills can you bring to the company that is relevant to their needs? Try to find the company that's the right fit for you, and you are much more likely to be what the company is looking for as well.
paragraphs.translation:
在申请实习时，既要考虑你能为公司带来什么，也要考虑公司能为你提供什么：
你能为公司带来哪些符合他们需求的技能组合？
尽量找到适合你的公司，这样你也更有可能成为该公司寻找的人选。

paragraphs.text: Knocking on doors can lead to fantastic opportunities: Designers are very busy and overwhelmed with people applying to work with them, but they're far more impressed by people that try that little bit harder. For example, some graduates go overseas to New York or Milan to deliver a self-directed design project and CV to the designer of their choice. Of course that can lead to considerable expense, but it often results in success.
paragraphs.translation:
主动登门拜访可以带来绝佳的机会：设计师们非常忙碌，面对大量求职者应接不暇，但他们对于那些付出更多努力的人印象要深刻得多。
例如，有些毕业生前往海外的纽约或米兰，向他们选定的设计师当面递交一份自主完成的设计项目和简历。
当然，这可能会产生相当可观的费用，但通常能带来成功。

paragraphs.text: Make use of online fashion and business networking sites. Create your profile on each one, as you never know who might be looking. Apply to as many fashion hiring agencies as you can - there are more than 20 in the UK alone. Not all of them take on new graduates, but try them all anyway.
paragraphs.translation:
利用在线时尚和商业社交网站。
在每个网站上创建个人资料，因为你永远不知道谁会看到它们。
尽可能多地申请时尚招聘机构——仅在英国就有超过20家。
并非所有机构都招聘应届毕业生，但无论如何还是都尝试一下。

paragraphs.text: Consider your training and fill in any gaps in it. Assistant designers and interns can make themselves more employable through investing time in obtaining, for example, computer-aided design (CAD) skills. Unfortunately, not all colleges and universities have CAD as an integral part of their courses. If this has affected you, you should study using online learning applications.
paragraphs.translation:
审视你的培训经历，并弥补其中的不足之处。
助理设计师和实习生可以通过投入时间获取例如计算机辅助设计（CAD）技能，从而提升自己的就业竞争力。
遗憾的是，并非所有学院和大学都将CAD作为课程的重要组成部分。
如果这影响到了你，你应该利用在线学习应用程序进行学习。

paragraphs.text: Finally, talent is not enough _ you need to get out there and make sure everybody knows about your skills. Graduates should be aware that they need to be proactive and persistent. It's all down to developing new contacts and utilising the ones you already have.
paragraphs.translation:
最后，仅凭天赋是不够的——你需要走出去，确保每个人都知道你的技能。
毕业生应该意识到他们需要积极主动并坚持不懈。
这一切都归结于拓展新的人脉并利用你已有的关系。

sentence_translations.sentence: First, it's important to think about what types of fashion designers are in demand currently.
sentence_translations.translation: 首先，思考当前哪些类型的时装设计师有需求是很重要的。

sentence_translations.sentence: There are so many womenswear designers, yet not as many menswear sportswear or accessories designers.
sentence_translations.translation: 女装设计师非常多，但男装、运动服或配饰设计师却没有那么多。

sentence_translations.sentence: Opportunities might be greater in those categories.
sentence_translations.translation: 这些类别中的机会可能更大。

sentence_translations.sentence: When applying for internships, think about what you'll bring to the company as well as what they can offer you:
sentence_translations.translation: 在申请实习时，既要考虑你能为公司带来什么，也要考虑公司能为你提供什么：

sentence_translations.sentence: Is the company going to teach you skills that are relevant to your future career?
sentence_translations.translation: 这家公司是否会教你与你未来职业相关的技能？

sentence_translations.sentence: What mix of skills can you bring to the company that is relevant to their needs?
sentence_translations.translation: 你能为公司带来哪些符合他们需求的技能组合？

sentence_translations.sentence: Try to find the company that's the right fit for you, and you are much more likely to be what the company is looking for as well.
sentence_translations.translation: 尽量找到适合你的公司，这样你也更有可能成为该公司寻找的人选。

sentence_translations.sentence: Knocking on doors can lead to fantastic opportunities: Designers are very busy and overwhelmed with people applying to work with them, but they're far more impressed by people that try that little bit harder.
sentence_translations.translation: 主动登门拜访可以带来绝佳的机会：设计师们非常忙碌，面对大量求职者应接不暇，但他们对于那些付出更多努力的人印象要深刻得多。

sentence_translations.sentence: For example, some graduates go overseas to New York or Milan to deliver a self-directed design project and CV to the designer of their choice.
sentence_translations.translation: 例如，有些毕业生前往海外的纽约或米兰，向他们选定的设计师当面递交一份自主完成的设计项目和简历。

sentence_translations.sentence: Of course that can lead to considerable expense, but it often results in success.
sentence_translations.translation: 当然，这可能会产生相当可观的费用，但通常能带来成功。

sentence_translations.sentence: Make use of online fashion and business networking sites.
sentence_translations.translation: 利用在线时尚和商业社交网站。

sentence_translations.sentence: Create your profile on each one, as you never know who might be looking.
sentence_translations.translation: 在每个网站上创建个人资料，因为你永远不知道谁会看到它们。

sentence_translations.sentence: Apply to as many fashion hiring agencies as you can - there are more than 20 in the UK alone.
sentence_translations.translation: 尽可能多地申请时尚招聘机构——仅在英国就有超过20家。

sentence_translations.sentence: Not all of them take on new graduates, but try them all anyway.
sentence_translations.translation: 并非所有机构都招聘应届毕业生，但无论如何还是都尝试一下。

sentence_translations.sentence: Consider your training and fill in any gaps in it.
sentence_translations.translation: 审视你的培训经历，并弥补其中的不足之处。

sentence_translations.sentence: Assistant designers and interns can make themselves more employable through investing time in obtaining, for example, computer-aided design (CAD) skills.
sentence_translations.translation: 助理设计师和实习生可以通过投入时间获取例如计算机辅助设计（CAD）技能，从而提升自己的就业竞争力。

sentence_translations.sentence: Unfortunately, not all colleges and universities have CAD as an integral part of their courses.
sentence_translations.translation: 遗憾的是，并非所有学院和大学都将CAD作为课程的重要组成部分。

sentence_translations.sentence: If this has affected you, you should study using online learning applications.
sentence_translations.translation: 如果这影响到了你，你应该利用在线学习应用程序进行学习。

sentence_translations.sentence: Finally, talent is not enough _ you need to get out there and make sure everybody knows about your skills.
sentence_translations.translation: 最后，仅凭天赋是不够的——你需要走出去，确保每个人都知道你的技能。

sentence_translations.sentence: Graduates should be aware that they need to be proactive and persistent.
sentence_translations.translation: 毕业生应该意识到他们需要积极主动并坚持不懈。

sentence_translations.sentence: It's all down to developing new contacts and utilising the ones you already have.
sentence_translations.translation: 这一切都归结于拓展新的人脉并利用你已有的关系。

paragraphs.text: The type of training provided in a business will depend on the resources available for training, the type of company, and the priority the company places on training.
paragraphs.translation: 企业提供的培训类型将取决于可用于培训的资源、公司类型以及公司对培训的重视程度。

paragraphs.text: Technical training is a type of training meant to teach the new employee the technological aspects of the job. For example, in a consulting business, technical training might be used so the consultant knows how to operate the system to input the number of hours that should be charged to a client. In a restaurant, the server might need to be trained on how to process customers' orders using a tablet.
paragraphs.translation:
技术培训旨在向新员工传授工作的技术层面知识。
例如，在咨询公司中，技术培训可能用于让顾问了解如何操作系统以输入应向客户收取的工时数。
在餐厅中，服务员可能需要接受培训，学习如何使用平板电脑处理顾客的订单。

paragraphs.text: In production focussed businesses, quality training involves familiarizing employees with the means of preventing, detecting, and eliminating non-quality products. In a world where quality can set your business apart from competitors, this type of training provides employees with the knowledge to recognize products that are not up to quality standards and teaches them what action to take in this scenario. This type of training can result in cost savings in production as well as provide an edge in the marketing of the product.
paragraphs.translation:
在以生产为导向的企业中，质量培训涉及让员工熟悉预防、检测和消除不合格产品的方法。
在一个质量能让你的企业脱颖而出的世界里，这种培训为员工提供了识别不符合质量标准的产品的知识，并教他们在这种情况下应采取何种行动。
这种培训可以降低生产成本，同时为产品的营销提供优势。

paragraphs.text: Skills training includes proficiencies needed to actually perform the job. For example, an administrative assistant might be trained in how to answer the phone, while a salesperson might be trained in assessment of customer needs and on how to offer the customer the necessary information to make a buying decision. A cashier needs to know not only the technology to ring something up on the till, but what to do if something has been given the wrong price.
paragraphs.translation:
技能培训包括实际执行工作所需的能力。
例如，行政助理可能接受接听电话的培训，而销售人员则可能接受评估客户需求以及如何向客户提供必要信息以做出购买决策的培训。
收银员不仅需要知道用收银机录入商品的技术，还需要知道商品被标错价格时该如何处理。

paragraphs.text: A fourth type of training is called 'soft skills' training. Soft skills refer to personality traits and personal habits that may influence relationships with other people. Executives say there is an increasing need for people who have not only the technical skills to do a job but also the necessary soft skills, such as being good at different types of communication, including listening to colleagues and customers. In a retail or restaurant environment, essential soft skills might include how to motivate others establish rapport and keep a conversation going. Skills such as these are used in every interaction with customers and are a key component of the customer experience.
paragraphs.translation:
第四种培训被称为‘软技能’培训。
软技能指的是可能影响人际关系的个性特征和个人习惯。
高管们表示，对于不仅具备工作所需的技术技能，还拥有必要软技能（例如擅长不同类型的沟通，包括倾听同事和客户）的人才的需求日益增长。
在零售或餐厅环境中，关键的软技能可能包括如何激励他人、建立融洽关系以及保持对话进行。
诸如此类的技能在每一次与客户的互动中都会用到，并且是客户体验的关键组成部分。

paragraphs.text: The small business lifecycle
paragraphs.translation: 小型企业的生命周期

paragraphs.text: From the moment you make the decision to set up a business, you're in the ‘business Lifecycle’. This will see you progress from idea to startup, and if successful, through to the growth and maturity phases.
paragraphs.translation:
从你决定创办一家企业的那一刻起，你就进入了‘商业生命周期’。
这将见证你从创意阶段推进到初创阶段，如果成功，还会经历成长和成熟阶段。

paragraphs.text: Stage 1 is lnitial Development. This is the very beginning of the business lifecycle. You've got your business idea and you're ready to take the plunge. But before you do this you should get as many opinions as possible from friends, family, colleagues, or any industry specialists you have access to, Ultimately, the success of your business will come down to your own abilities, the state of the market and, of course, the decisions you make about the source of finance for your startup.
paragraphs.translation:
第一阶段是初始开发阶段。
这是商业生命周期的起点。
你已经有了商业想法，准备冒险一试。
但在你这样做之前，应该从朋友、家人、同事或你能接触到的任何行业专家那里尽可能多地获取意见。
最终，你企业的成功将取决于你自身的能力、市场状况，当然，还有你关于初创资金来源所做的决策。

paragraphs.text: Once you're satisfied that your idea is ready to go, you move on to Stage 2, which is Startup. Many believe this is the riskiest stage of the entire lifecycle, since mistakes made then can have an impact many years later. Based on the feedback from your first customers, you have to be ready to adapt your product or service. It can even get to the point where you are making so many changes to it that you start to feel a bit confused about what you're doing. Don't worry-this feeling will soon disappear as your company develops.
paragraphs.translation:
一旦你确信自己的想法已准备就绪，就可以进入第二阶段，即初创阶段。
许多人认为这是整个生命周期中风险最高的阶段，因为当时所犯的错误可能会在多年后产生影响。
根据首批客户的反馈，你必须准备好调整你的产品或服务。
甚至可能达到这样的程度：你对产品做了太多改动，以至于开始对自己所做的事情感到有些困惑。
别担心——随着公司的发展，这种感觉很快就会消失。

paragraphs.text: Stage 3 is Establishment. You should now be seeing your profits improve slowly and steadily, but you may struggle to divide the time available to you between the growing demands of your business. Employing the right people is essential, so you need to take a major part in recruitment, It is your job now to start establishing order and cohesion as you mobilize your team according to clearly defined and communicated goals.
paragraphs.translation:
第三阶段是成立期。
你现在应当看到利润在缓慢而稳定地增长，但你可能会难以将有限的时间分配在日益增长的业务需求之间。
雇佣合适的人员至关重要，因此你需要在招聘中承担主要角色。
现在你的职责是开始建立秩序和凝聚力，同时根据明确界定并传达的目标来调动你的团队。

paragraphs.text: By Stage 4, Expansion, you may see rapid growth in profits and wish to move forward. However, you need to be aware of the risks of expanding too carelessly, and should keep an eye on how far expansion might affect the quality of what you provide to your existing customers.
paragraphs.translation:
到了第四阶段，即扩张阶段，你可能会看到利润快速增长，并希望向前迈进。
然而，你需要意识到过于草率扩张的风险，并密切关注扩张在多大程度上可能影响你为现有客户提供的服务质量。

paragraphs.text: Stage 5 is Maturity, Here you may wish to further expand the business. Many companies in this situation bring in a new leader at this stage, to face the new challenges. Other entrepreneurs may decide that they should sell the company at this stage, and move on to a new project.
paragraphs.translation:
第五阶段是成熟期，此时你可能希望进一步拓展业务。
许多处于这种情况的公司会在这一阶段引入一位新的领导者，以应对新的挑战。
其他企业家可能决定在这一阶段出售公司，并转向新的项目。

evidence: But before you do this you should get as many opinions as possible from friends, family, colleagues, or any industry specialists you have access to

sentence_translations.sentence: The type of training provided in a business will depend on the resources available for training, the type of company, and the priority the company places on training.
sentence_translations.translation: 企业提供的培训类型将取决于可用于培训的资源、公司类型以及公司对培训的重视程度。

sentence_translations.sentence: Technical training is a type of training meant to teach the new employee the technological aspects of the job.
sentence_translations.translation: 技术培训旨在向新员工传授工作的技术层面知识。

sentence_translations.sentence: For example, in a consulting business, technical training might be used so the consultant knows how to operate the system to input the number of hours that should be charged to a client.
sentence_translations.translation: 例如，在咨询公司中，技术培训可能用于让顾问了解如何操作系统以输入应向客户收取的工时数。

sentence_translations.sentence: In a restaurant, the server might need to be trained on how to process customers' orders using a tablet.
sentence_translations.translation: 在餐厅中，服务员可能需要接受培训，学习如何使用平板电脑处理顾客的订单。

sentence_translations.sentence: In production focussed businesses, quality training involves familiarizing employees with the means of preventing, detecting, and eliminating non-quality products.
sentence_translations.translation: 在以生产为导向的企业中，质量培训涉及让员工熟悉预防、检测和消除不合格产品的方法。

sentence_translations.sentence: In a world where quality can set your business apart from competitors, this type of training provides employees with the knowledge to recognize products that are not up to quality standards and teaches them what action to take in this scenario.
sentence_translations.translation: 在一个质量能让你的企业脱颖而出的世界里，这种培训为员工提供了识别不符合质量标准的产品的知识，并教他们在这种情况下应采取何种行动。

sentence_translations.sentence: This type of training can result in cost savings in production as well as provide an edge in the marketing of the product.
sentence_translations.translation: 这种培训可以降低生产成本，同时为产品的营销提供优势。

sentence_translations.sentence: Skills training includes proficiencies needed to actually perform the job.
sentence_translations.translation: 技能培训包括实际执行工作所需的能力。

sentence_translations.sentence: For example, an administrative assistant might be trained in how to answer the phone, while a salesperson might be trained in assessment of customer needs and on how to offer the customer the necessary information to make a buying decision.
sentence_translations.translation: 例如，行政助理可能接受接听电话的培训，而销售人员则可能接受评估客户需求以及如何向客户提供必要信息以做出购买决策的培训。

sentence_translations.sentence: A cashier needs to know not only the technology to ring something up on the till, but what to do if something has been given the wrong price.
sentence_translations.translation: 收银员不仅需要知道用收银机录入商品的技术，还需要知道商品被标错价格时该如何处理。

sentence_translations.sentence: A fourth type of training is called 'soft skills' training.
sentence_translations.translation: 第四种培训被称为‘软技能’培训。

sentence_translations.sentence: Soft skills refer to personality traits and personal habits that may influence relationships with other people.
sentence_translations.translation: 软技能指的是可能影响人际关系的个性特征和个人习惯。

sentence_translations.sentence: Executives say there is an increasing need for people who have not only the technical skills to do a job but also the necessary soft skills, such as being good at different types of communication, including listening to colleagues and customers.
sentence_translations.translation: 高管们表示，对于不仅具备工作所需的技术技能，还拥有必要软技能（例如擅长不同类型的沟通，包括倾听同事和客户）的人才的需求日益增长。

sentence_translations.sentence: In a retail or restaurant environment, essential soft skills might include how to motivate others establish rapport and keep a conversation going.
sentence_translations.translation: 在零售或餐厅环境中，关键的软技能可能包括如何激励他人、建立融洽关系以及保持对话进行。

sentence_translations.sentence: Skills such as these are used in every interaction with customers and are a key component of the customer experience.
sentence_translations.translation: 诸如此类的技能在每一次与客户的互动中都会用到，并且是客户体验的关键组成部分。

sentence_translations.sentence: The small business lifecycle
sentence_translations.translation: 小型企业的生命周期

sentence_translations.sentence: From the moment you make the decision to set up a business, you're in the ‘business Lifecycle’.
sentence_translations.translation: 从你决定创办一家企业的那一刻起，你就进入了‘商业生命周期’。

sentence_translations.sentence: This will see you progress from idea to startup, and if successful, through to the growth and maturity phases.
sentence_translations.translation: 这将见证你从创意阶段推进到初创阶段，如果成功，还会经历成长和成熟阶段。

sentence_translations.sentence: Stage 1 is lnitial Development.
sentence_translations.translation: 第一阶段是初始开发阶段。

sentence_translations.sentence: This is the very beginning of the business lifecycle.
sentence_translations.translation: 这是商业生命周期的起点。

sentence_translations.sentence: You've got your business idea and you're ready to take the plunge.
sentence_translations.translation: 你已经有了商业想法，准备冒险一试。

sentence_translations.sentence: But before you do this you should get as many opinions as possible from friends, family, colleagues, or any industry specialists you have access to,
sentence_translations.translation: 但在你这样做之前，应该从朋友、家人、同事或你能接触到的任何行业专家那里尽可能多地获取意见。

sentence_translations.sentence: Ultimately, the success of your business will come down to your own abilities, the state of the market and, of course, the decisions you make about the source of finance for your startup.
sentence_translations.translation: 最终，你企业的成功将取决于你自身的能力、市场状况，当然，还有你关于初创资金来源所做的决策。

sentence_translations.sentence: Once you're satisfied that your idea is ready to go, you move on to Stage 2, which is Startup.
sentence_translations.translation: 一旦你确信自己的想法已准备就绪，就可以进入第二阶段，即初创阶段。

sentence_translations.sentence: Many believe this is the riskiest stage of the entire lifecycle, since mistakes made then can have an impact many years later.
sentence_translations.translation: 许多人认为这是整个生命周期中风险最高的阶段，因为当时所犯的错误可能会在多年后产生影响。

sentence_translations.sentence: Based on the feedback from your first customers, you have to be ready to adapt your product or service.
sentence_translations.translation: 根据首批客户的反馈，你必须准备好调整你的产品或服务。

sentence_translations.sentence: It can even get to the point where you are making so many changes to it that you start to feel a bit confused about what you're doing.
sentence_translations.translation: 甚至可能达到这样的程度：你对产品做了太多改动，以至于开始对自己所做的事情感到有些困惑。

sentence_translations.sentence: Don't worry-this feeling will soon disappear as your company develops.
sentence_translations.translation: 别担心——随着公司的发展，这种感觉很快就会消失。

sentence_translations.sentence: Stage 3 is Establishment.
sentence_translations.translation: 第三阶段是成立期。

sentence_translations.sentence: You should now be seeing your profits improve slowly and steadily, but you may struggle to divide the time available to you between the growing demands of your business.
sentence_translations.translation: 你现在应当看到利润在缓慢而稳定地增长，但你可能会难以将有限的时间分配在日益增长的业务需求之间。

sentence_translations.sentence: Employing the right people is essential, so you need to take a major part in recruitment.
sentence_translations.translation: 雇佣合适的人员至关重要，因此你需要在招聘中承担主要角色。

sentence_translations.sentence: It is your job now to start establishing order and cohesion as you mobilize your team according to clearly defined and communicated goals.
sentence_translations.translation: 现在你的职责是开始建立秩序和凝聚力，同时根据明确界定并传达的目标来调动你的团队。

sentence_translations.sentence: By Stage 4, Expansion, you may see rapid growth in profits and wish to move forward.
sentence_translations.translation: 到了第四阶段，即扩张阶段，你可能会看到利润快速增长，并希望向前迈进。

sentence_translations.sentence: However, you need to be aware of the risks of expanding too carelessly, and should keep an eye on how far expansion might affect the quality of what you provide to your existing customers.
sentence_translations.translation: 然而，你需要意识到过于草率扩张的风险，并密切关注扩张在多大程度上可能影响你为现有客户提供的服务质量。

sentence_translations.sentence: Stage 5 is Maturity, Here you may wish to further expand the business.
sentence_translations.translation: 第五阶段是成熟期，此时你可能希望进一步拓展业务。

sentence_translations.sentence: Many companies in this situation bring in a new leader at this stage, to face the new challenges.
sentence_translations.translation: 许多处于这种情况的公司会在这一阶段引入一位新的领导者，以应对新的挑战。

sentence_translations.sentence: Other entrepreneurs may decide that they should sell the company at this stage, and move on to a new project.
sentence_translations.translation: 其他企业家可能决定在这一阶段出售公司，并转向新的项目。

parts.title: Passage 3
parts.article_title: The nursery that took all the children's toys away

paragraphs.text: Do toys stifle children's creativity? One Munich nursery decided to find out. Sarah Jewell reports
paragraphs.translation:
玩具会扼杀孩子的创造力吗？
慕尼黑的一家托儿所决定对此进行探究。
莎拉·朱厄尔报道

paragraphs.text: Children are ready consumers, particularly of toys. Their toy chests may be bursting but they are still desperate for the latest doll or train set. Depriving children of their toys seems unkind, yet a growing number of nurseries in Germany do just this. For three months of the year they put away their toys and all that is left to play with are the tables, chairs and a few blankets.
paragraphs.translation:
儿童是天生的消费者，尤其是在玩具方面。
他们的玩具箱可能已经塞满，但他们仍然渴望拥有最新的洋娃娃或火车套装。
剥夺孩子的玩具似乎不太友善，但德国越来越多的幼儿园正是这样做的。
每年有三个月，他们会收起玩具，留给孩子们玩的只剩下桌子、椅子和几条毯子。

paragraphs.text: The project is called Der Spielzeugfreie Kindergarten (the nursery without toys) and was founded by Rainer Strick and Elke Schubert, public health officers who worked with adults suffering from various forms of addiction. They were concerned about the addictive habits that start early in childhood and wanted to show that children can play happily and creatively when they are not being 'suffocated' by their toys.
paragraphs.translation:
该项目被称为“无玩具幼儿园”（Der Spielzeugfreie Kindergarten），由公共卫生官员雷纳·斯特里克和埃尔克·舒伯特创立，他们曾与患有各种成瘾症的成年人打交道。
他们担忧童年早期就开始形成的成瘾习惯，并希望证明，当孩子们不被玩具“窒息”时，他们能够快乐且富有创造性地玩耍。

paragraphs.text: One of the nurseries that has been following this project for the past two years is the Friedrich-Engels-Bogen nursery in Munich. Gisela Marti, a teacher there, says: ‘In these three months we offer the children space and time to get to know the mselves.’ The aim is to make the children 'self-confident, able to bear conflict and frustration, able to say "yes" as well as "no" and also aware of their weaknesses and strengths'. According to Gisela Marti, the children's day is deliberately unstructured as one of the basic beliefs of the project is that children spend too much time being rushed around from one activity to another and they end up with a 'reduced space for life'. The children are encouraged to do what they want, in their own way.
paragraphs.translation:
过去两年一直在实施这一项目的其中一所幼儿园是慕尼黑的弗里德里希·恩格斯弧线幼儿园。
那里的老师吉塞拉·马尔蒂说：“在这三个月里，我们给孩子们提供空间和时间来了解他们自己。”
目标是让孩子们变得“自信、能够承受冲突和挫折、既会说“是”也会说“不”，并且意识到自己的弱点和优势”。
据吉塞拉·马尔蒂所说，孩子们的一天被故意安排得没有固定结构，因为该项目的基本信念之一就是孩子们花费太多时间被催促着从一个活动赶到另一个活动，最终导致他们“生活空间被压缩”。
孩子们被鼓励按照自己的方式做他们想做的事情。

paragraphs.text: A video taken of the children during the three-month toy-free period shows them on the first day staring at each other hesitantly and looking apprehensively around the big, empty classroom. One of the nursery teachers, Gudrun Huber, says: ‘We left them alone, even if they were bored, because sometimes things in life are boring and you have to learn to cope.’ On the second day the children are filmed playing with the chairs and blankets. They make a den by draping the blankets over the tables and weighing them down with shoes, and then they start running around the room, chatting and laughing excitedly, Gudrun Huber explains how this put them in an entirely different mood: ‘Once the children realised they could do what they liked and they were in control, they really went a bit mad - they got very boisterous and excited, climbing all over the furniture.’ Initially it was difficult for the staff, not just because it was unbearably noisy, but because, as Gudrun Huber says: ‘It was difficult to hold back and let the children be.’
paragraphs.translation:
一则记录孩子们在三个月无玩具期间的视频显示，第一天他们犹豫地相互凝视，并忧虑地环顾宽敞空荡的教室。
一位幼儿园老师古德伦·胡贝尔说：“我们让他们独自待着，即使他们感到无聊，因为生活中有些事本就乏味，你必须学会应对。”
第二天，孩子们被拍到用椅子和毯子玩耍。
他们用毯子盖在桌子上并用鞋子压住，搭成一个窝，然后开始在房间里奔跑，兴奋地聊天大笑。古德伦·胡贝尔解释道，这让他们进入了一种完全不同的情绪：“一旦孩子们意识到他们可以做自己喜欢的事并掌握主动权，他们确实有点疯狂——变得非常喧闹和激动，到处攀爬家具。”
起初这对员工来说很困难，不仅仅是因为无法忍受的吵闹，还因为正如古德伦·胡贝尔所说：“很难克制自己并让孩子们自由发挥。”

paragraphs.text: Like Gudrun Huber, Gisela Marti found it hard to re-evaluate the rules she was used to: 'They weren't allowed to do anything really dangerous, but they were allowed to jump on the chairs and tables, and that is not something they would normally be allowed to do. As a teacher you do have to have confidence in the children.' But she adds: ‘Everyone has to work within their own boundaries and some teachers will allow more dangerous and active play than others.’
paragraphs.translation:
像古德伦·胡贝尔一样，吉塞拉·马蒂发现很难重新评估她习惯的规则：“他们不允许做任何真正危险的事，但可以跳上椅子和桌子，而这通常是不被允许的。”
作为老师，你确实必须对孩子们有信心。”
但她补充道：“每个人都必须在自己设定的范围内行事，有些老师会比其他人允许更危险和活跃的游戏。”

paragraphs.text: Gisela Marti found that once the children settled down to the new regime, they invented games: ‘They loved acting and putting on a show, or pretending to be in a circus or on a train, but most importantly, all the time they were playing, they were learning to socialise.’
paragraphs.translation: 吉塞拉·马蒂发现，一旦孩子们适应了新的规则，他们便开始发明游戏：‘他们喜欢表演和演出，或者假装在马戏团或火车上，但最重要的是，他们在玩耍的过程中一直在学习社交。’

paragraphs.text: Two weeks before the end of the project the teachers and children had a group discussion about which toys they would like brought back. The children were happy to get their toys back, but they were also aware that they had fun without them. As one little boy in Gudrun Huber's class said: ' like having no toys because then you can use your imagination instead.
paragraphs.translation:
在项目结束前的两周，老师和孩子们进行了一次小组讨论，讨论他们希望带回哪些玩具。
孩子们很高兴能拿回玩具，但他们也意识到，没有玩具时他们同样玩得很开心。
正如古德伦·胡贝尔班上一个小男孩所说：“我喜欢没有玩具，因为那样你就可以发挥想象力了。”

paragraphs.text: At the end of the project, Elke Schubert thought there were definite benefits. ‘We find that children on the project concentrate better when they work, integrate better into groups and communicate better than the children who didn't take part.’
paragraphs.translation:
在项目结束时，埃尔克·舒伯特认为有明确的好处。
“我们发现，参与项目的儿童在工作时注意力更集中，更好地融入群体，并且比未参与项目的儿童沟通能力更强。”

paragraphs.text: The parents were also positive about how the 'time without toys' affected their children. Some parents have even copied the nursery's example. As one father said: 'Klaus used to get out all his toys and spread them all over the room and they got in such a mess that he wasn't playing properly with any of them. So we put all the toys away in the cellar and now we only get out what he actually wants to play with and he gets much less frustrated.'
paragraphs.translation:
家长们也对“无玩具时间”如何影响他们的孩子持积极态度。
一些家长甚至效仿了这家幼儿园的做法。
正如一位父亲所说：“克劳斯以前会把他所有的玩具都拿出来，摊得满屋子都是，弄得一团糟，以至于他哪个玩具都没好好玩。”
所以，我们把所有玩具都收进了地下室，现在只拿出他真正想玩的玩具，他的挫败感也少多了。”

paragraphs.text: Elsa Davies is Director of the National Playing Fields Association. She says: ‘The most natural and durable learning happens through play and often play which is freely chosen by the child. Teachers often underestimate the power of that learning.’
paragraphs.translation:
埃尔莎·戴维斯是国家运动场协会的主任。
她表示：‘最自然且持久的学习是通过游戏发生的，而这种游戏往往是孩子自由选择的。
教师常常低估了这种学习的力量。’

questions.analysis: 题干询问Gisela Marti对幼儿园的批评点。原文第四段提到，该项目的基本理念之一是‘孩子们花太多时间被匆忙地从一个活动赶到另一个活动’，导致‘生活空间被压缩’。这表明她批评的是幼儿园过度安排、组织过多，对应选项D中的‘the amount of organisation children are exposed to there’。其他选项在文中均无直接依据。

parts.source_article_title: The nursery that took all the children's toys away

sentence_translations.sentence: Do toys stifle children's creativity?
sentence_translations.translation: 玩具会扼杀孩子的创造力吗？

sentence_translations.sentence: One Munich nursery decided to find out.
sentence_translations.translation: 慕尼黑的一家托儿所决定对此进行探究。

sentence_translations.sentence: Sarah Jewell reports
sentence_translations.translation: 莎拉·朱厄尔报道

sentence_translations.sentence: Children are ready consumers, particularly of toys.
sentence_translations.translation: 儿童是天生的消费者，尤其是在玩具方面。

sentence_translations.sentence: Their toy chests may be bursting but they are still desperate for the latest doll or train set.
sentence_translations.translation: 他们的玩具箱可能已经塞满，但他们仍然渴望拥有最新的洋娃娃或火车套装。

sentence_translations.sentence: Depriving children of their toys seems unkind, yet a growing number of nurseries in Germany do just this.
sentence_translations.translation: 剥夺孩子的玩具似乎不太友善，但德国越来越多的幼儿园正是这样做的。

sentence_translations.sentence: For three months of the year they put away their toys and all that is left to play with are the tables, chairs and a few blankets.
sentence_translations.translation: 每年有三个月，他们会收起玩具，留给孩子们玩的只剩下桌子、椅子和几条毯子。

sentence_translations.sentence: The project is called Der Spielzeugfreie Kindergarten (the nursery without toys) and was founded by Rainer Strick and Elke Schubert, public health officers who worked with adults suffering from various forms of addiction.
sentence_translations.translation: 该项目被称为“无玩具幼儿园”（Der Spielzeugfreie Kindergarten），由公共卫生官员雷纳·斯特里克和埃尔克·舒伯特创立，他们曾与患有各种成瘾症的成年人打交道。

sentence_translations.sentence: They were concerned about the addictive habits that start early in childhood and wanted to show that children can play happily and creatively when they are not being 'suffocated' by their toys.
sentence_translations.translation: 他们担忧童年早期就开始形成的成瘾习惯，并希望证明，当孩子们不被玩具“窒息”时，他们能够快乐且富有创造性地玩耍。

sentence_translations.sentence: One of the nurseries that has been following this project for the past two years is the Friedrich-Engels-Bogen nursery in Munich.
sentence_translations.translation: 过去两年一直在实施这一项目的其中一所幼儿园是慕尼黑的弗里德里希·恩格斯弧线幼儿园。

sentence_translations.sentence: Gisela Marti, a teacher there, says: ‘In these three months we offer the children space and time to get to know the mselves.’
sentence_translations.translation: 那里的老师吉塞拉·马尔蒂说：“在这三个月里，我们给孩子们提供空间和时间来了解他们自己。”

sentence_translations.sentence: The aim is to make the children 'self-confident, able to bear conflict and frustration, able to say "yes" as well as "no" and also aware of their weaknesses and strengths'.
sentence_translations.translation: 目标是让孩子们变得“自信、能够承受冲突和挫折、既会说“是”也会说“不”，并且意识到自己的弱点和优势”。

sentence_translations.sentence: According to Gisela Marti, the children's day is deliberately unstructured as one of the basic beliefs of the project is that children spend too much time being rushed around from one activity to another and they end up with a 'reduced space for life'.
sentence_translations.translation: 据吉塞拉·马尔蒂所说，孩子们的一天被故意安排得没有固定结构，因为该项目的基本信念之一就是孩子们花费太多时间被催促着从一个活动赶到另一个活动，最终导致他们“生活空间被压缩”。

sentence_translations.sentence: The children are encouraged to do what they want, in their own way.
sentence_translations.translation: 孩子们被鼓励按照自己的方式做他们想做的事情。

sentence_translations.sentence: A video taken of the children during the three-month toy-free period shows them on the first day staring at each other hesitantly and looking apprehensively around the big, empty classroom.
sentence_translations.translation: 一则记录孩子们在三个月无玩具期间的视频显示，第一天他们犹豫地相互凝视，并忧虑地环顾宽敞空荡的教室。

sentence_translations.sentence: One of the nursery teachers, Gudrun Huber, says: ‘We left them alone, even if they were bored, because sometimes things in life are boring and you have to learn to cope.’
sentence_translations.translation: 一位幼儿园老师古德伦·胡贝尔说：“我们让他们独自待着，即使他们感到无聊，因为生活中有些事本就乏味，你必须学会应对。”

sentence_translations.sentence: On the second day the children are filmed playing with the chairs and blankets.
sentence_translations.translation: 第二天，孩子们被拍到用椅子和毯子玩耍。

sentence_translations.sentence: They make a den by draping the blankets over the tables and weighing them down with shoes, and then they start running around the room, chatting and laughing excitedly, Gudrun Huber explains how this put them in an entirely different mood: ‘Once the children realised they could do what they liked and they were in control, they really went a bit mad - they got very boisterous and excited, climbing all over the furniture.’
sentence_translations.translation: 他们用毯子盖在桌子上并用鞋子压住，搭成一个窝，然后开始在房间里奔跑，兴奋地聊天大笑。古德伦·胡贝尔解释道，这让他们进入了一种完全不同的情绪：“一旦孩子们意识到他们可以做自己喜欢的事并掌握主动权，他们确实有点疯狂——变得非常喧闹和激动，到处攀爬家具。”

sentence_translations.sentence: Initially it was difficult for the staff, not just because it was unbearably noisy, but because, as Gudrun Huber says: ‘It was difficult to hold back and let the children be.’
sentence_translations.translation: 起初这对员工来说很困难，不仅仅是因为无法忍受的吵闹，还因为正如古德伦·胡贝尔所说：“很难克制自己并让孩子们自由发挥。”

sentence_translations.sentence: Like Gudrun Huber, Gisela Marti found it hard to re-evaluate the rules she was used to: 'They weren't allowed to do anything really dangerous, but they were allowed to jump on the chairs and tables, and that is not something they would normally be allowed to do.'
sentence_translations.translation: 像古德伦·胡贝尔一样，吉塞拉·马蒂发现很难重新评估她习惯的规则：“他们不允许做任何真正危险的事，但可以跳上椅子和桌子，而这通常是不被允许的。”

sentence_translations.sentence: As a teacher you do have to have confidence in the children.'
sentence_translations.translation: 作为老师，你确实必须对孩子们有信心。”

sentence_translations.sentence: But she adds: ‘Everyone has to work within their own boundaries and some teachers will allow more dangerous and active play than others.’
sentence_translations.translation: 但她补充道：“每个人都必须在自己设定的范围内行事，有些老师会比其他人允许更危险和活跃的游戏。”

sentence_translations.sentence: Gisela Marti found that once the children settled down to the new regime, they invented games: ‘They loved acting and putting on a show, or pretending to be in a circus or on a train, but most importantly, all the time they were playing, they were learning to socialise.’
sentence_translations.translation: 吉塞拉·马蒂发现，一旦孩子们适应了新的规则，他们便开始发明游戏：‘他们喜欢表演和演出，或者假装在马戏团或火车上，但最重要的是，他们在玩耍的过程中一直在学习社交。’

sentence_translations.sentence: Two weeks before the end of the project the teachers and children had a group discussion about which toys they would like brought back.
sentence_translations.translation: 在项目结束前的两周，老师和孩子们进行了一次小组讨论，讨论他们希望带回哪些玩具。

sentence_translations.sentence: The children were happy to get their toys back, but they were also aware that they had fun without them.
sentence_translations.translation: 孩子们很高兴能拿回玩具，但他们也意识到，没有玩具时他们同样玩得很开心。

sentence_translations.sentence: As one little boy in Gudrun Huber's class said: ' like having no toys because then you can use your imagination instead.
sentence_translations.translation: 正如古德伦·胡贝尔班上一个小男孩所说：“我喜欢没有玩具，因为那样你就可以发挥想象力了。”

sentence_translations.sentence: At the end of the project, Elke Schubert thought there were definite benefits.
sentence_translations.translation: 在项目结束时，埃尔克·舒伯特认为有明确的好处。

sentence_translations.sentence: “We find that children on the project concentrate better when they work, integrate better into groups and communicate better than the children who didn't take part.”
sentence_translations.translation: “我们发现，参与项目的儿童在工作时注意力更集中，更好地融入群体，并且比未参与项目的儿童沟通能力更强。”

sentence_translations.sentence: The parents were also positive about how the 'time without toys' affected their children.
sentence_translations.translation: 家长们也对“无玩具时间”如何影响他们的孩子持积极态度。

sentence_translations.sentence: Some parents have even copied the nursery's example.
sentence_translations.translation: 一些家长甚至效仿了这家幼儿园的做法。

sentence_translations.sentence: As one father said: 'Klaus used to get out all his toys and spread them all over the room and they got in such a mess that he wasn't playing properly with any of them.
sentence_translations.translation: 正如一位父亲所说：“克劳斯以前会把他所有的玩具都拿出来，摊得满屋子都是，弄得一团糟，以至于他哪个玩具都没好好玩。”

sentence_translations.sentence: So we put all the toys away in the cellar and now we only get out what he actually wants to play with and he gets much less frustrated.'
sentence_translations.translation: 所以，我们把所有玩具都收进了地下室，现在只拿出他真正想玩的玩具，他的挫败感也少多了。”

sentence_translations.sentence: Elsa Davies is Director of the National Playing Fields Association.
sentence_translations.translation: 埃尔莎·戴维斯是国家运动场协会的主任。

sentence_translations.sentence: She says: ‘The most natural and durable learning happens through play and often play which is freely chosen by the child.
sentence_translations.translation: 她表示：‘最自然且持久的学习是通过游戏发生的，而这种游戏往往是孩子自由选择的。

sentence_translations.sentence: Teachers often underestimate the power of that learning.’
sentence_translations.translation: 教师常常低估了这种学习的力量。’
